description:
Evaluate documentation rendering options (Docsify, MDBook, Jekyll, etc.) and implement chosen solution before v1.0 release.

## Goal

Provide professional, searchable documentation site for v1.0 users while maintaining markdown source for agent accessibility.

## Key Requirements

- Full-text search across all documentation
- Professional appearance and navigation
- Preserve markdown source files (agent-readable)
- Minimal maintenance overhead
- GitLab Pages compatible

## Deliverables

- Evaluation of all viable options (see attached document)
- Decision made and documented
- Chosen solution implemented
- Documentation hosted and accessible
- Maintenance process documented

See attached document for detailed option analysis and recommendation (Docsify).

---

## Resolution (Rejected 2026-07-02)

External static docs site is out of v1.0 scope.

**Decision:** v1.0 does not owe external human readers a hosted, searchable docs site. JIT is CLI-first, repository-local, and agent-oriented; agents and developers consume the Diátaxis markdown in `docs/` directly, and the web UI (`jit serve` + DocumentViewer) already covers the internal/operator doc-viewing case.

**Why not fold into the web UI:** The web UI renders any `docs/` file but is a live server, not a static artifact, and would still need (a) search widened beyond issue-linked docs, and (b) a docs-tree nav. Rejecting in favor of the web UI would relocate the work plus add server-hosting burden, so nothing is built instead.

**Evaluation preserved:** `dev/studies/documentation-tooling-evaluation.md` (Docsify recommended) remains for if/when an external static site is reconsidered post-v1.0 — see the Doc Phase 2 epic (94f873c8).
title: Evaluate and implement documentation tooling for v1.0
